studyMaterials.title: Mastering the Quadratic Formula: Step-by-Step Derivation
studyMaterials.description: Learn how the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a is derived from completing the square, with 3 real worked examples.
studyMaterials.content:
# The Quadratic Formula & Derivation

The standard quadratic equation takes the form:
**ax² + bx + c = 0** (where a ≠ 0)

### Method: Completing the Square
1. Divide through by a:
   x² + (b/a)x + (c/a) = 0
2. Move the constant term to the right side:
   x² + (b/a)x = -c/a
3. Add (b / 2a)² to both sides to complete the square:
   x² + (b/a)x + (b / 2a)² = (b² / 4a²) - (c/a)
   [x + (b/2a)]² = (b² - 4ac) / 4a²
4. Take square roots of both sides:
   x + (b/2a) = ± √(b² - 4ac) / 2a
5. Subtract b/2a:
   **x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a)**

### Key Discriminant Rules (Δ = b² - 4ac)
- **Δ > 0**: Two distinct real roots.
- **Δ = 0**: Exactly one repeated real root (perfect square).
- **Δ < 0**: No real roots (complex roots).

studyMaterials.title: Ohm's Law & Circuit Analysis Cheat Sheet
studyMaterials.description: Quick reference for Voltage, Current, Resistance, and Electrical Power relationships (V = IR, P = VI = I²R = V²/R).
studyMaterials.content:
# Ohm's Law & DC Power Formulas

### The Fundamental Triangle
- **V = I × R** (Voltage = Current in Amperes × Resistance in Ohms)
- **I = V / R**
- **R = V / I**

### Electrical Power Calculations
- **P = V × I** (Watts = Volts × Amps)
- **P = I² × R** (Joule heating loss in cables)
- **P = V² / R**

### Practical Application: Solar Inverter Sizing
If a residential inverter supplies **3000 Watts (3kW)** at **240V AC**, the AC current drawn is:
I = P / V = 3000W / 240V = **12.5 Amps**.

On the DC 48V battery side (assuming 90% inverter efficiency):
Total DC Power = 3000 / 0.90 = 3333W.
DC Current = 3333W / 48V = **69.4 Amps**.
*Rule of thumb:* Always size battery DC cable conductors for minimum 70A to prevent excessive voltage drops!

studyMaterials.title: Newton's Laws of Motion & Momentum Conservation
studyMaterials.description: Concise summary of the three laws of motion, inertia, friction factors, and impulse-momentum equations with exam tips.
studyMaterials.content:
# Newton's Three Laws of Motion

### 1. First Law (Law of Inertia)
An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in uniform straight-line motion stays in motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

### 2. Second Law (Force & Acceleration)
The rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force and occurs in the direction of the force:
**F_net = m × a** (Force in Newtons = Mass in kg × Acceleration in m/s²)

### 3. Third Law (Action & Reaction)
For every action force exerted on body B by body A, there is an equal in magnitude and opposite in direction reaction force exerted on body A by body B.
*Important:* Action and reaction forces act on **two different objects**, which is why they never cancel each other out!

studyMaterials.title: Python Core Syntax & Data Structures Quickstart

# Python Core Syntax Reference

### Data Structures
```python
# List (Ordered, mutable)

# Dictionary (Key-value mapping)

    "name": "Wuse Electrical",

}

```

### Loops & List Comprehensions


quizzes.title: Algebraic Equations & Quadratic Roots Drill
quizzes.description: Test your grasp on solving linear systems, factorizing quadratics, and evaluating discriminants.

questions.question: What are the roots of the quadratic equation x² - 7x + 12 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factoring: (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0. Therefore x = 3 or x = 4. Check: 3² - 7(3) + 12 = 9 - 21 + 12 = 0.

questions.question: If the discriminant (b² - 4ac) of a quadratic equation is strictly negative (Δ < 0), what can be said about the roots?
options: The equation has two equal rational roots
The equation has two distinct real roots
The equation has no real roots (the roots are complex)
The equation has exactly one zero root
questions.explanation: Because the quadratic formula requires taking the square root of the discriminant, √(negative number) produces complex/imaginary roots, meaning there are no intersections on the real x-axis.

questions.question: Solve for x: 3(2x - 4) = 4x + 6.
questions.explanation: Expand: 6x - 12 = 4x + 6. Subtract 4x from both sides: 2x - 12 = 6. Add 12: 2x = 18. Divide by 2: x = 9.

quizzes.title: Electrical Principles & Circuit Safety Drill
quizzes.description: Fundamental questions on current flow, Ohm’s Law, inverter power calculations, and household protective devices.

questions.question: If a 240V electric water heater has an internal element resistance of 20 Ohms, what current does it draw from the mains?
questions.explanation: By Ohm’s Law, Current I = V / R = 240V / 20Ω = 12 Amperes.

questions.question: Which protective safety device trips within milliseconds specifically when it senses electrical leakage current to ground, protecting human life from lethal shock?
options: RCD / GFCI (Residual Current Device / Ground Fault Interrupter)
questions.explanation: An RCD (Residual Current Device) or GFCI detects small current imbalances (typically 30mA or less) between live and neutral wires and disconnects power to prevent fatal electrocution.

questions.question: In a residential solar system, what is the primary role of a Charge Controller?
options: Converting DC battery voltage into 220V AC voltage
Regulating voltage and current from solar panels to protect batteries from overcharging
Switching between NEPA/PHCN utility power and generator automatically
Measuring the water level in lead-acid battery cells
questions.explanation: Solar Charge Controllers (MPPT or PWM) regulate incoming power from photovoltaic arrays to safely charge storage batteries without overheating or overcharging them.

quizzes.title: Newtonian Mechanics & Force Dynamics
quizzes.description: Test your understanding of Newton’s second law, friction, acceleration due to gravity, and momentum conservation.

questions.question: A constant horizontal force of 50 N is applied to accelerate a 10 kg crate across a frictionless floor. What is the acceleration produced?
questions.explanation: Using Newton’s second law: a = F / m = 50 N / 10 kg = 5.0 m/s².

questions.question: True or False: Action and reaction forces described in Newton’s third law cancel each other out because they are equal and opposite.
questions.explanation: False! Action and reaction forces act on TWO DIFFERENT bodies, so they never cancel each other out on any single isolated object.
